questions.prompt: When graphing $y < 2x + 1$, the boundary line should be:
hints: Points on the line are not included.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: Strict inequalities use a dashed line.

questions.prompt: To graph $y \ge x^2 - 1$, you first draw the parabola $y = x^2 - 1$ as a ___ line.
hints: The boundary is part of the solution.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: Because of ≥, the line is solid.

questions.prompt: Is $(0,0)$ a solution of $y \ge x^2 - 1$? (Enter yes or no)
The graph of $x > -2$ is a vertical line with shading to the:
hints: Right side has larger x values.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: Shade to the right of the vertical line.

questions.prompt: When an inequality is $y > mx + b$, you shade ___ the line.
hints: Larger y means higher on the graph.

questions.prompt: For $x \ge 5$, is the boundary line solid or dashed?
The solution of a system of inequalities is the:
options: A. Union of all shaded regions
B. Intersection of all shaded regions
hints: They must be in each shaded region.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: It's the overlap (intersection) of the shaded regions.

questions.prompt: Vertices of a solution region are found by solving ___ of boundary equations.
In the system $x - y < 2$, $x > -2$, $y \le 3$, what is the $x$-coordinate of the vertex at the intersection of $x = -2$ and $y = 3$? (Enter a number)
If an intersection point does not satisfy all original inequalities, it is plotted as:
To find intersection points of a parabola and a line, you set the expressions for $y$ ___ and solve for $x$.
hints: You equate the two right-hand sides.
Same as solving a system of equations.

questions.prompt: In the nonlinear system $x^2 - y \le 1$, $-x + y \le 1$, one intersection point is $(-1,0)$. What is the $y$-coordinate of the other? (Enter a number)
hints: Look at the $y$ of the second intersection.

questions.prompt: A system of inequalities with no overlapping shaded region has:
hints: If shading doesn't overlap, no point satisfies all.

questions.prompt: In the work schedule problem, the feasible region is a triangle with vertices $(0,16)$, $(0,20)$, and $(___ ,0)$.

A company makes two products, each requiring time on two machines. The constraints form a feasible region that is a quadrilateral. The vertices of this region are usually found by solving pairs of constraint equations. (True or False)
hints: Vertices are intersections of constraint boundaries.
questions.feedbackIfWrong: True. The vertices are found by solving the intersecting lines.
